newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Oil steadies after investment funds spark drop.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Oil steadies after investment funds spark drop.

text.p: World oil prices steadied on Wednesday as traders re-evaluated the market after Tuesday's heavy price slump.
London futures for bellwether North Sea Brent blend closed up just one cent at $19.23 a barrel after falling 78 cents on Tuesday.
Dealers were sifting through market factors after investment funds joined a wholesale sell-off sparked by a report showing the market full to the limit with long positions.
"People are taking a fresh look at the market and trying to decide whether the speculative money might come back in and provide some sort of bounce," said a trader.
They said a weekly report on U.S. oil inventories, out after futures markets close on Wednesday, would provide fresh clues on the vital status of the country's gasoline stocks.

"Stocks are definitely on the rise but as of today they are still low in terms of days of forward demand cover by historical standards," said Mohammad Abduljabbar, senior economist at Washington's Petroleum Finance Corp.

Brent crude had rallied $1 a barrel in the two weeks before Tuesday as U.S. refineries ratcheted up gasoline production in preparation for the unofficial start of the peak summer driving season, traditionally marked by Monday's Memorial Day holiday.
But dealers now are divided on whether U.S. gasoline can sustain oil prices at levels still running nearly $3 higher on average this year than in the four years from 1991-1995 after the Gulf War.
While U.S. gasoline stocks remain nearly seven million barrels below levels seen this time last year, demand in 1997 is expected to rise a mere 0.3 percent.
